title: Compromise speed limit plan for residential streets
subtitle: Federal retrofit grant bids, Uptown water feature contract, strategic plan mission workshop, and new Button Factory washroom funding.
overview: After two earlier speed proposals failed on tied votes, Council approved a revised plan for lower speed limits on residential streets {{vote:m12}}. In Wards 1 to 6, school zones go to 30 km/h, local roads and minor collectors to 40 km/h, and major collectors stay at 50 km/h. Ward 7 gets its own plan with 30 km/h on local roads as well as school zones. Staff will begin implementation in spring 2023 and report back each year, and the Traffic and Parking By-law will be updated.

Council also approved three federal grant applications for recreation facility retrofits, with the City's share of up to $9,980,000 committed if any succeed. It released funding for a new Button Factory universal washroom and for AMCC design work, and awarded the Uptown water feature and plaza contract. Each of these passed unanimously.

Council held a workshop on a new mission statement for the 2023-2026 Strategic Plan, with the next public session set for April 1 at RIM Park. A closed session on council orientation was held earlier in the day, and the minutes report no decisions from it.

decisions.detail: Council approved a revised Option 2b plan with 30 km/h school zones, 40 km/h local and minor collector roads and 50 km/h major collectors in Wards 1-6, plus a Ward 7 plan with 30 km/h on local roads, starting in spring 2023 {{vote:m12}}.

decisions.item: Green and Inclusive Community Buildings grants
decisions.detail: Council approved applications for RIM Park, Albert McCormick and Moses Springer retrofits, and committed up to $9,980,000 in City funding if any are successful.

decisions.item: Uptown water feature and plaza contract
decisions.detail: Council awarded tender RFT22-26 to Ghent Landscape for a total of $1,693,608.05 and released $1,366,000 in 2023 capital funding for the Waterloo Public Square Water Feature.
Council released $250,000 in 2023 capital funding to build a new universal washroom at the Button Factory.
Council released $158,000 in 2023 non-routine funding so staff can start design work for the AMCC upgrades and reconfiguration.
Council received the report on the second strategic plan workshop and asked each member to review the pre-read material for it.

debate: Councillors who backed a 40 km/h base speed said residents wanted a limit they could comply with, and that signs at 40 now could be changed later at lower cost. They also cited feedback from their constituents against 30 km/h.

Supporters of 30 km/h on local streets said it improves safety and builds a culture of slower driving. They argued the extra commute time is small and pointed to results from other cities. A neighbourhood association delegate also supported 30 km/h on safety and policy grounds.

Staff said a City pilot of lower limits showed no change in collisions and no reported road-rage concerns. Reductions in actual driving speeds are typically only one to three km/h. Staff warned that lower posted limits could increase traffic-calming requests and costs, and said it is hard to tell school zones apart if all streets are 30 km/h.

Several councillors raised concerns about the Ward 7 plan. One said that many Ward 7 school zones sit on bisected streets without boulevards. Staff preferred a consistent city-wide approach but said a ward-specific plan was possible.
Both earlier motions failed on tied votes. After a recess, staff drafted a combined motion with a separate Ward 7 plan, which passed.
